guidance.value: Double-digit growth for the full year

highlights: Added 26 gross stores in Q2 and 53 in H1; total store count reached 844 across 582 cities.

Vishal Mega Mart Ltd.whatChanged: Versus Q1FY27 revenue growth of 18.7% and SSSG of 10%, Q2 revenue growth was 14% and reported SSSG was 5.4% amid the festival shift; management maintained confidence in double-digit full-year SSSG and more than 100 FY27 openings.
risks: Festival buying shifted into Q3, reducing Q2 fixed-cost absorption; Q2 EBITDA margin declined 80 bps YoY and H1 margin declined 30 bps.
Raw-material inflation remained elevated; management said it had already made selective price changes and was protecting opening price points and customer affordability.
Minimum-wage increases raised employee costs; management estimated 8–10% SSSG is needed to offset this pressure, alongside new-store costs and festival timing.

sectorSummary.overview: Value retail remained expansion-led, but the festival shift into Q3 slowed reported same-store growth and exposed uneven demand. Vishal remained confident, V-Mart saw festive trading below expectations, and V2 made next-year expansion conditional on a recovery.

trends.text: Festive buying shifted from Q2 to Q3, reducing reported same-store growth; management-adjusted growth is distinct from reported performance.
Store additions continued to drive scale even as same-store demand softened.

tailwinds.text: Management expects the shifted festive season to support Q3 sales comparisons.
Smaller-city expansion remains a growth opportunity, with further stores planned this year.

headwinds.text: Input-cost inflation requires sourcing efficiencies, changes in assortment or selective price increases to preserve affordability.
V-Mart and V2 reported pressure on underlying consumer demand beyond the calendar effect.

opportunities.text: V-Mart sees further upside from Unlimited productivity and the integration of LimeRoad with store inventory.
Vishal is testing Belong & Co. while expanding its South India footprint; the new format remains a pilot.

risks.text: V2’s inventory and borrowings increased with front-loaded expansion; recovery in store productivity is important before further acceleration.
V-Mart faces intense competition in its eastern and central-northern markets alongside wage and sourcing-cost pressure.

insights.text: Vishal attributed most Q2 same-store growth to market-share gains rather than existing customers buying more.
V2 retained its FY27 revenue-growth ambition but reduced its full-year same-store growth expectation and may slow FY28 openings if Q3 disappoints.
